chunks: Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā narrated from Ibrāhīm ibn ʿUmar, from Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him), who said:
Whoever says three times: ‘Glory be to my Lord, the Great, and praise be to Him. I seek forgiveness from my Lord and turn penitently to Him,’ the Throne is struck as a chain strikes a bowl.

key_terms.سُبْحَانَ رَبِّيَ الْعَظِيمِ: Glory be to my Lord, the Great
key_terms.وَأَتُوبُ إِلَيْهِ: and I turn penitently to Him

ai.seo_question: What is the reward of reciting 'Subhana Rabbiyal Azeem' three times?
ai.summary: In the Shia tradition of *kitab-al-zuhd*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) emphasizes the profound cosmic impact of sincere repentance, likening the auditory resonance of the Throne to a chain striking a bowl to signify the weight of the believer's plea. This metaphor underscores the immediacy and magnitude of divine acceptance, linking personal spiritual practice to the structural reality of the heavens.
